title: AI lesson 2: how AI chat assistants work

linkedin.media_title: AI lesson 2: how chat assistants work
linkedin.text:
Most people use AI chat every day without knowing what is happening behind the box. Lesson 2 of 100 in AI from zero.

Three steps, no jargon:

1. It read a huge library. Books, websites, code. From that it learned patterns in how language fits together.

2. Your words become tokens. Your question is cut into small pieces, a word or part of a word each.

3. It predicts the reply one piece at a time. Each step, it picks the most likely next piece, until the answer is done.

That third step explains the thing that trips everyone up: AI predicts likely words, not checked facts. So it can sound completely sure and still be wrong, or invent a source that doesn't exist.

That doesn't make it useless. It makes you the editor. Let it draft, then you check.

Your 2-minute task: ask an AI something you already know the answer to. Then ask it how sure it is and where the information comes from. Notice what it admits.
